newsitem.title: UK: European stocks, dollar slip after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: European stocks, dollar slip after U.S. data.

text.p: European stocks slid on U.S. data suggesting the strong U.S. economy was starting to show a pick up in inflation.

The dollar briefly hit a session high against the mark after the U.S. said July nonfarm payrolls jumped 316,000, pushing the unemployment rate down to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June. A Reuters survey had predicted a 193,000-payrolls gain and a 4.9 percent jobless rate.
But the dollar slipped off its peak after a strong National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) report showed the manufacturing sector remaining strong but now, amid higher price pressures.
NAPM's July index of manufacturing activity rose to 58.6 from June's 55.7 A Reuters survey had expected July NAPM at 56.1.

But traders were more concerned with the NAPM prices paid component, which rose to 53.6 to post its first move above 50 in four months. An index above 50 is often seen as a sign of expansion while a figure below 50 is seen as a contraction.

"We had two warning signals today," said Robert Dederick, economic consultant at Northern Trust Co. "One in the employment report, which suggested that pressures in the labor market are there with no sign of abatement and another in this report, which shows that manufacturing is not devoid of capacity stress."
Any signs of inflation amid a strong U.S. economy is likely to spark fears the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on August 19.
The strong payrolls gain initially sent U.S. government bond prices tumbling, which sent long-term rates higher and pressured Wall Street at the open.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average recouped its losses within the first half hour with help from firm technology stocks and a flat hourly earnings component in the labor report.
Average hourly earnings remained at $12.23 per hour in July while the average workweek slipped to 34.4 hours from June's 34.7, indicating little wage inflation threat.
But U.S. bond prices extended losses and the Dow fell sharply in midafternoon after the NAPM report. The Dow was off 89.43 points at 8,133.18 at 1500 GMT.
Weakness in U.S. markets quickly rippled through Europe and sent government bonds and stocks markets lower.
London's FTSE-100 and Paris' CAC-40 indices swiftly dropped into negative ground to session lows.

German shares also slipped, with the IBIS DAX index shedding about 100 points, or more than two percent, in electronic trading. German shares also suffered as investors sold stock before the weekend to lock in profits made in the recent rally to record peaks.
Daimler-Benz AG was among the weakest shares after two investment banks cut their earnings estimates for the company.

Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgraded Daimler's 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates despite the company's more than doubling of its operating profit in its six-month earnings report. At midday, Daimler shares were down 5.90 marks at 148.90 but off its sessiojn low of 147.20 in the afternoon.
Switzerland's bourse is closed for a holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8570 marks and 118.00 yen from 1.8380 and 118.40 yen in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 12.7points at 4,894.80.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended down 30.14 points in bourse trade at 4,408.79. The IBIS DAX was down 68.54 points at 4,336.98 in electronic trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 26.23 points at 3,049.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at 1500 GMT at $324.10, down from Thursday's close at $324.90. ($ = 7.989 Swedish Crowns) ($ = 2.079 Dutch Guilders)
